entities.summary: Elizabeth Eleanor Siddall, better known as Elizabeth Siddal, was an English artist, art model, and poet. Siddal was perhaps the most significant of the female models who posed for the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood. Their ideas of female beauty were fundamentally influenced and personified by her. Walter Deverell and William Holman Hunt painted Siddal, and she was the model for John Everett Millais's famous painting Ophelia (1852). Early in her relationship with Dante Gabriel Rossetti, Siddal became his muse and exclusive model, and he portrayed her in almost all his early artwork depicting women.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Elizabeth Siddal's influence on Pre-Raphaelite art and her association with Dante Gabriel Rossetti significantly impacted the development of Victorian-era aesthetics. Her legacy can be seen in the works of subsequent artists, including John Everett Millais.
